title: Record the characteristic polynomial of A_1 on the 128-dimensional dihedral isotypic component
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->

## Change and mathematical scope

Exact characteristic polynomial of `A_1` on the 128-dimensional isotypic component `W` of the two-dimensional rational representation of the order-12 dihedral image inside the `c=1` joint `(+1,+1)` space.

```text
chi_{A_1, W}(x) = q(x)^2
q(x) = x^6 (x-2)^4 (x+2)^4 f(x) g(x) h(x) k(x)
```

`f` and `g` are the published degree-11 pair, `h` and `k` the published degree-14 pair, with `g(x) = -f(-x)` and `k(x) = h(-x)`. Ascending-coefficient SHA256 of `chi_{A_1, W}` is `bf10fad08aa427ff461bc3a7a7377f5b90ab7a810a1004d81e550a2a328bbb65`.

Evidence class: finite exact linear algebra over `Q`, one characteristic polynomial. The selected conditional kappa remains `781451/250000000`. This PR does not edit the selected frontier.

Remaining: geometric multiplicity of eigenvalue 0 on `W` (algebraic multiplicity 12), and an explicit matrix of the multiplicity-space operator `T` whose characteristic polynomial is `q`.

## Task and overlap

Base commit `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`. Catalogue card `formal-interface-lemma`, scope changed: the card asks for a formal binding, and this package answers the polynomial left open by PR #7023. Live inputs are the historical `INTERFACE.json`, the pinned 216-dimensional basis, and the pinned matrix of `B = 4 A_1`.

Overlap search on 2026-11-10, open-PR snapshot 10:16:36Z (339 records, pagination complete) and discussion snapshot 10:17:43Z (7013 records, pagination complete). Local notes 10178 committed paths at that base, complete. The phrases `128-dimensional isotypic`, `two-dimensional rational`, `isotypic component` and `multiplicity 64` matched only PR #7023 and discussion comment 19514162, both of which list this polynomial as remaining. A later open-PR search for `128-dimensional isotypic` returned only #7023.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library.

```sh
python3 -B -W error research/a1-isotypic-128-charpoly/verify.py
python3 -B -O research/a1-isotypic-128-charpoly/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a1-isotypic-128-charpoly --check-only
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a1-isotypic-128-charpoly
```

Marker `PASS_A1_ISOTYPIC_128_CHARPOLY`. Metadata check `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. Registered replay `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. Selected-baseline orientation `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.

The verifier rebuilds the query, the dihedral presentation, the 216-dimensional basis, the projector `6P` (trace 768, rank 128, `(6P)^2 = 6(6P)`), a unimodular Hermite basis, and the integer matrix of `B`. Determinant samples at `0, 1, 2, 3, 5` match the Hessenberg characteristic polynomial. Rejection controls cover a transposed coordinate, a partial swap of coordinates 4 and 7, a swapped port label, a nearby permutation of `r`, a dropped character coefficient, dropping `g` and `t`, and a one-entry change of the integer matrix.

No Lean, Docker, degree-881 replay, or selected cold replay was run.

## Credit

JoyboyBrian recorded the sign-character dimensions. PR #6944 supplied the 216-dimensional blocks. PR #6964 computed the degree-216 polynomial, basis and matrix. PR #7008 identified `r`, `u` and multiplicity 64. PR #7023 proved the 8-dimensional summand is reducible and asked this question. Ali Romman's PR #4958 and PR #4720 retain the query and the Bell action. Nick Petalas's PR #5120 is the degree-410 lower bound. Krzysztof Wojt's `research/exact-one-slot-gram/` is the degree-881 annihilator. The doubled representation comes from PR #1719.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. New work is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

See `research/a1-isotypic-128-charpoly/TASK.json`.

- Exact rational rank of `B`, `B-8I` and `B+8I` on `W`.
- An explicit integer matrix of the multiplicity-space operator `T`.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The pinned degree-216 basis and matrix made the restriction a finite check rather than another search. One suggested improvement is a shared importable form of the `c=1` symmetry and port-action routines, so a successor package can replay them without copying `research/a1-joint-216-charpoly/verify.py`. Feedback discussion: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200
